sections.title: Triangle Centers: Centroid, Incenter, Circumcenter, Orthocenter
sections.content:
1. Centroid (G): Intersection of medians.
Formula: G = ((x1 + x2 + x3)/3 , (y1 + y2 + y3)/3)
Example (3 steps): A(0,0), B(6,0), C(0,6)
Step 1: Add x-coordinates = 6
Step 2: Add y-coordinates = 6
Step 3: G = (2,2)

2. Incenter: Intersection of angle bisectors. Coordinates depend on side lengths.

3. Circumcenter: Intersection of perpendicular bisectors. In a right triangle, it is the midpoint of the hypotenuse.

4. Orthocenter: Intersection of altitudes. In a right triangle, it is the vertex of the right angle.

sections.title: Perpendicular Distance from Point to Line
sections.content:
Distance from point (x1,y1) to line ax + by + c = 0:
|ax1 + by1 + c| / √(a² + b²)

Example (4 steps): Point (1,2), Line 3x + 4y − 5 = 0
Step 1: Substitute → 3(1) + 4(2) − 5 = 6
Step 2: Denominator = √(9 + 16) = 5
Step 3: Distance = 6/5
Step 4: Final answer = 6/5 units

Distance between parallel lines:
|c1 − c2| / √(a² + b²)

sections.title: Reflection of a Point
sections.content:
1. Across x-axis: (x, y) → (x, −y)
2. Across y-axis: (x, y) → (−x, y)
3. Across line y = x: (x, y) → (y, x)

General reflection across ax + by + c = 0:
x' = x − 2a(ax + by + c)/(a² + b²)
y' = y − 2b(ax + by + c)/(a² + b²)

Example (3 steps): Reflect (2,3) across x-axis
Step 1: Keep x same
Step 2: Change sign of y
Step 3: Image = (2, −3)

sections.title: Circle: Standard and General Form
sections.content:
Standard form: (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r²
General form: x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0
Center = (−g, −f)
Radius = √(g² + f² − c)

Example (4 steps): x² + y² − 4x − 6y − 3 = 0
Step 1: Compare with general form → g = −2, f = −3
Step 2: Center = (2,3)
Step 3: r = √(4 + 9 + 3)
Step 4: r = 4

sections.title: Length of Tangent from External Point
sections.content:
If circle equation is S = 0, then tangent length from point (x1,y1) is √S1
Where S1 = x1² + y1² + 2gx1 + 2fy1 + c

Example (4 steps): Substitute point in S1
Step 1: Put values in S1
Step 2: Compute value
Step 3: Take square root
Step 4: Final tangent length

sections.title: Basic Locus Problems
sections.content:
If a point moves at a fixed distance r from origin, locus is:
x² + y² = r²

If a point is equidistant from two fixed points, locus is the perpendicular bisector of the line joining them.

Example (3 steps): Distance from origin = 5
Step 1: r = 5
Step 2: Equation = x² + y² = 25
Step 3: Represents a circle centered at (0,0)

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 focuses on triangle centers, point-line distance, reflections, circle properties, tangent length, and basic locus equations. Always convert geometric meaning into algebraic form and solve in 3–4 logical steps.

tricks.title: Centroid Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Just take average of all three x’s and y’s.

tricks.title: Orthocenter in Right Triangle
tricks.explanation: Vertex of right angle is orthocenter.
tricks.example: If angle A is 90°, orthocenter is A

tricks.title: Point to Line Distance Memory Tip
tricks.explanation: Put point in numerator, √(a²+b²) in denominator.

tricks.title: Reflection Quick Rule
tricks.explanation: Change sign of coordinate depending on axis.

tricks.title: Tangent Length Trick
tricks.explanation: Substitute point in S and take square root.

tricks.title: Locus Recognition
tricks.explanation: Fixed distance → circle; Equal distance from two points → perpendicular bisector.
